toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Dr Marrable: this looks like one chance QC outlier, not a fault in Analyzer B or the new reagent lot. The repeat of the same vial passed. Sodium and chloride were fine in the same run. Level 2 averages are unchanged after the lot change. Every scheduled QC ran on time, so the short-staffing theory is not supported. Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed with Analyzer B within 0.02 mmol/L on average, and the patient moving median was normal. A one-in-300 flag a few times a month is expected. A sampling glitch is possible, but nobody can confirm it, so don't record it as the cause.

The Ward 6 highs are not explained by analyzer error. Half were run on Analyzer A. Most had over 3 hours' delay in transit because the tube station is down, and the ward took four renal overflow patients. Delayed samples tend to read high. That link is plausible but not proven.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the 186-result review with no amendments. Do not recall results, widen limits or quarantine the lot. Add temporary extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 for fresh repeat samples on current highs, and get the tube station fixed. I'm fairly confident, and I collected no further evidence.
